records.title: Morescient GAI for Software Engineering (Extended Version)
records.rationale: A vision/roadmap for semantics-aware generative code models and observation platforms; it concerns LLMs in SE but involves no agents, no multi-agent orchestration, and no empirical comparison, so it is only background on trustworthiness limits of code models.

records.title: Software Engineering for Collective Cyber-Physical Ecosystems
records.rationale: The 'collectives' here are self-organising swarm/CPS devices and macroprogramming abstractions, not LLM-based agents; this is a classical multi-agent/self-organisation paper and falls under the non-LLM-agent exclusion.

records.title: Foundation Model Engineering: Engineering Foundation Models Just as Engineering Software
records.rationale: Proposes applying SE methodology to building foundation models (SE4FM), the inverse direction of this review; no agents, orchestration, or failure-mode evidence, so it serves only as framing for treating models as engineered artifacts.

records.title: Insights from the Frontline: GenAI Utilization Among Software Engineering Students
records.rationale: An interview study of SE students using ChatGPT/Copilot as assistive tools; it is empirical and LLM-related but concerns education and human tool use rather than autonomous or multi-agent LLM systems.

records.title: A Survey of Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning with Communication
records.rationale: Surveys communication mechanisms in multi-agent deep reinforcement learning; the agents are RL policies rather than LLMs, matching the explicit exclusion for non-LLM agents despite the coordination-relevant framing.

records.title: An Exploratory Study of V-Model in Building ML-Enabled Software: A Systems Engineering Perspective
records.rationale: Studies V-Model process adoption and interdisciplinary human collaboration for ML-enabled systems; there are no LLM agents and the 'collaboration' analyzed is between practitioners, not agent roles.

records.title: Trustworthy and Synergistic Artificial Intelligence for Software Engineering: Vision and Roadmaps
records.rationale: A Future-of-SE roadmap on trustworthy AI4SE that predates agentic frameworks; useful for framing trustworthiness challenges but offers no architecture, benchmark, or agent failure-mode data.

records.title: Performance of Genetic Algorithms in the Context of Software Model Refactoring
records.rationale: Compares NSGA-II/PESA2 genetic algorithms for search-based model refactoring; entirely non-LLM and unrelated to agent orchestration.

records.title: The Evolving Landscape of Software Performance Engineering
records.rationale: Industrial lessons on performance engineering under CI/CD with no LLM or agent component; the shared keyword is 'engineering', not agentic systems.

records.title: The Present and Future of Bots in Software Engineering
records.rationale: A 2022 themed-issue introduction on rule-triggered SE bots that predates LLM agents; relevant only as historical background on automation actors embedded in developer workflows.

records.title: Text and Team: What Article Metadata Characteristics Drive Citations in Software Engineering?
records.rationale: A bibliometric regression on title/abstract metadata and citation counts in SE venues; no LLM agents and no bearing on any research question.

records.title: A Catalogue of Evaluation Metrics for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Frameworks in Software Engineering
records.rationale: A metrics catalogue for LLM multi-agent frameworks in SE speaks directly to RQ3's 'how are they measured' clause and supplies the measurement vocabulary needed to compare architectures across studies.

records.title: Towards LLM-augmented multiagent systems for agile software engineering
records.rationale: Sketches a cognitive MAS+LLM ecosystem mapped onto Agile practice; it contributes an architectural proposal for role-based SE agents but the truncated abstract shows no evaluation or single-agent baseline.

records.title: ScholForge: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Autonomous Software Engineering Research
records.rationale: A named hierarchical multi-agent system whose stage-specialized agents illustrate role decomposition, but the target activity is conducting research rather than the SE lifecycle tasks the RQs center on.

records.title: Multi-LLM Agent Collaborative Intelligence
records.rationale: MACI orchestrates multiple LLM agents specifically to compensate for single-model weaknesses in long-range planning, self-critique, and context loss; the failure modes named generalize to SE coordination even though the book is domain-agnostic.

records.title: Demystifying LLM-Based Software Engineering Agents
records.rationale: A dedicated review of LLM SE agents spanning code synthesis, repair, and test generation across both research and industry practice, which is the closest match in this chunk to RQ1's survey-of-the-landscape framing.

records.title: StarVerus: LLM-Powered Multi-Agent Collaboration for Industrial Rust Code Verification Automation
records.rationale: An industrial multi-agent system for generating Rust/Verus specifications gives a concrete verification-oriented architecture, but the abstract shows no single-agent contrast or coordination failure analysis to answer an RQ directly.

records.title: Engineering LLM Powered Multi-Agent Framework for Autonomous CloudOps
records.rationale: Metadata-only record, but the title unambiguously names an LLM multi-agent framework for cloud operations, an in-scope SE activity; the 21 citations suggest a usable architecture reference despite the missing abstract.

records.title: A Multi-Agent RAG Framework for Regulatory Compliance Checking of Software Requirements
records.rationale: Applies a multi-agent RAG pipeline to requirements compliance checking, contributing a requirements-phase architecture and an evaluation setting, though the framing is manual-inspection replacement rather than multi- versus single-agent comparison.

records.title: Understanding Conversational Patterns in Multi-agent Programming: A Case Study on Fibonacci Game Development
records.rationale: Explicitly studies how LLM agents coordinate and maintain role adherence during a programming task, which is exactly the coordination-failure evidence RQ3 asks for even though the case study is small.

records.title: Fairness in Multi-Agent Systems for Software Engineering: An SDLC-Oriented Rapid Review
records.rationale: A rapid review mapping LLM/MAS use across the SDLC, which yields a useful phase-by-phase inventory; the fairness lens is a non-functional concern adjacent to, rather than part of, the coordination and reliability questions.

records.title: A Validation and Governance Framework for Multi-Agent LLM Scientific Software Development
records.rationale: Targets run-to-run non-determinism in multi-agent LLM development and critiques synthetic-test benchmarks as inadequate validation, addressing RQ3's verification and reliability measurement problem head-on.

records.title: SGAgent: Suggestion-Guided LLM-Based Multi-Agent Framework for Repository-Level Software Repair
records.rationale: A named multi-agent repair framework operating at repository scale, likely benchmarked on SWE-bench-style tasks; valuable as an architecture and results source but the abstract promises no single-agent ablation.

records.title: Bridging Design and Implementation: A Study of Multi-Agent LLM Architectures for Automated Front-End Generation
records.rationale: Compares multi-agent architectures for multimodal design-to-code generation, contributing architectural variants for one SE task; the stated gap is modality coverage rather than the conditions under which specialization pays off.

records.title: SALLMA: A Software Architecture for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
records.rationale: Metadata-only SATrends paper, but the title names a reference software architecture for LLM multi-agent systems, making it a citable architectural contribution for the design-space discussion.

records.title: Towards Role-Based Multi-Agent LLM Systems for Software Requirements Analysis
records.rationale: Role specialization applied to requirements analysis matches the review's central construct, but with no abstract available there is no evidence of a comparative baseline, so it stands as an architectural exemplar.

records.title: Developing Multi-Agent LLM Applications Through Continuous Human-LLM Co-Programming
records.rationale: Addresses the engineering process for building multi-agent LLM applications with a human in the loop, contributing development-practice insight rather than performance or failure-mode evidence.

records.title: A Multi-Agent LLM Environment for Software Design and Refactoring: A Conceptual Framework
records.rationale: A conceptual multi-agent framework covering design and refactoring, two lifecycle phases under-represented relative to code generation; conceptual-only status keeps it below core.

records.title: SE-Blackboard: A Shared-State Architecture for Multi-Agent Software Engineering Pipelines
records.rationale: A blackboard shared-state design targets the context-loss and handoff problems that plague agent pipelines, making it a directly relevant coordination mechanism; the record carries only journal metadata, so it is retained as an architecture rather than as RQ evidence.

records.title: Enhancing LLM Code Generation: A Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Agent Collaboration and Runtime Debugging for Accuracy, Reliability, and Latency
records.rationale: Promoted above its rank because the title states a systematic empirical evaluation of multi-agent collaboration measured on accuracy, reliability, and latency, which is precisely the cost-versus-benefit trade-off RQ2 poses.

records.title: AI-Powered Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Unit Test Case Generation: Enhancing Software Quality through LLM’s
records.rationale: A multi-agent framework for unit test generation covers the testing activity in scope and supplies an application data point, though the metadata-only record shows no comparative or failure-mode analysis.

records.title: Demystifying LLM-Based Software Engineering Agents: A Review of Capabilities, Benchmarks, and Failure Modes
records.rationale: The snippet quantitatively compares resolution rate, cost, and failure modes and states that multi-agent frameworks overcome single-agent limitations through roles, hitting RQ2 and RQ3 simultaneously; it may be the extended version of 10.1145/3715754 and should be checked for duplication at full-text retrieval.

records.title: Multi-Agent Systems for Software Development: a Multi-Faceted Research Question-driven Reference Guide
records.rationale: The snippet contrasts specialised coordinated agents against a single-agent backbone system (SWE-agent style) and catalogues capabilities, limitations, and design trade-offs, giving direct RQ2 comparative material despite its low rank.
